If sentiment is >0.67 in the last 3 days and forecast is trending down, increase the next 3-day forecast by 1.5–2.5% to counteract downward bias.  
If sentiment is <0.33 and forecast is trending up, reduce the next 3-day forecast by 1.5–2.5% to avoid over-optimism.  
In mid-horizon (days 10–20), if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast deviates >2% from true, apply a linear correction toward the true path with slope = 0.8 * (true - forecast).  
Late horizon (days 20–30), if sentiment is >0.67 and forecast is below true, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.  
Early horizon (days 1–5), if sentiment is >0.67 and forecast is above true, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overreaction to bullish sentiment.  
If sentiment is >0.67 and forecast is flat, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to reflect sentiment-driven upward bias.
